headline: The Tamagotchi was invented by an office worker who wanted a pet she could carry.
slides: Aki Maita worked in marketing at Bandai. She developed it with toy designer Akihiro Yokoi of WiZ.
Before launch she handed prototypes to high school girls in Shibuya and changed it based on what they said.
It went on sale in Japan. In the US on May 1, 1997, for about $18.
Roughly 40 million were sold in the first year or so. Plenty of schools banned them.
Maita and Yokoi won the 1997 Ig Nobel Prize in economics, for diverting millions of hours of work into virtual pets.
Over 91 million have been sold. You can still buy a new one.
